wordmark.purpose: The name WHEELMAN in the top bar: Montserrat 800, uppercase, Carbarn Blue. Used nowhere else.

headline.purpose: The one sentence in the empty conversation that says how many are waiting.

title.purpose: The open conversation's name, the car's name at the top of the panel (line-height 1.2), the panel title without tabs, "Wheelman now", the AI dialog's title, the empty-list heading.

body.purpose: Default text and message bubbles; list names at 500, rising to 650 when unanswered.

editor.purpose: The draft in the message box and the paste box: line-height 1.5 for editing.

ui.purpose: List previews, chips, segments, section tabs (500; 650 when selected), Customer-tab rows, the quiet panel, the viewer caption.

label.purpose: Status pill, notices, header sub-line, car strip, thread pills, advice lines, fine print.

label-strong.purpose: Section headings in the panel and status panel (Navy Ink), the "Suggested reply" label, bubble sender lines, small and mini buttons, blank buttons.

caption.purpose: Times in the list and in bubbles, badge numerals (700), tags (650), the word count, the written-at time, Find a car meta, the photo count chip, a document kind.

mono.purpose: AI model names in the status panel and the AI dialog only.

shadows.name: shadow-1
shadows.purpose: Resting lift: bubbles, date and event pills, the message box, the quiet panel, the paste box, the sticky Load older button, the selected segment of a switch (light only).

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: Floating: the jump-to-newest button, the toast, the panel as a drawer, the status panel, the Find a car results, the AI dialog.

shadows.name: shadow-1-dark
shadows.purpose: Resting lift in the dark theme (same custom property, redefined). The selected segment has none in dark.

shadows.name: shadow-2-dark
shadows.purpose: Floating in the dark theme (same custom property, redefined).

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Behind the AI dialog; rgba(0, 0, 0, .55) in dark. The viewer uses its own near-black ground as its backdrop.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Press feedback, the toast, the jump button, photos and the draft arriving, the viewer, the tab underline.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The panel sliding in as a drawer at 1279px and under.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Press scale (0.97 buttons, chips and segments; 0.94 icon buttons, the jump button and the viewer arrows; 0.96 blank and back buttons), colour and border changes, the toast and the jump button appearing, the play disc growing under the pointer.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: A new suggestion fading in from a 2px blur; the strip thumbnail, the main photo and the viewer picture arriving; the viewer opening; the section tab underline scaling in; the drawer fading from 60% opacity; photo tiles zooming 4% under the pointer.

motion.name: dur-drawer
motion.purpose: The drawer's slide from the right; the main photo zooming 2% under the pointer.

motion.name: busy-dot
motion.purpose: Status dot pulsing to 35% opacity while checking or writing.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: The "check now" icon while a check runs.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Loading bars in the message box, skeleton rows in the list, the main photo while it is read.

motion.name: toast-dwell
motion.purpose: A toast stays 65ms per character, at least 2.6s and at most 14s; with Undo it stays 9s and takes clicks.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration token is 0ms and the looping animations (busy dot, spin, shimmer, arriving draft, loading photo) are switched off. Nothing animates.

breakpoints.name: drawer
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the panel leaves the grid and becomes a fixed drawer on the right (26rem); crossing below closes it.

breakpoints.name: compact-bar
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: "by Carbarn", the status chevron and "Open listing" on the car strip are hidden; Find a car narrows to 11rem.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: one column, list or conversation; the brand shows only its mark; the section tabs drop to a second row and hide while a conversation is open; Find a car waits behind a search icon; back button with a count; the draft maxes at 20dvh.

layout.frame: body.shell is a flex column the height of the window; the document does not scroll
layout.topBar: min-height 3.5rem; grid: brand | tabs (minmax(0, 1fr)) | Find a car | status, cog, check now

columns.list: minmax(20rem, 25rem); minmax(20rem, 22rem) while the panel is open
columns.panel: 26rem (only while open; a drawer at 1279px and under)

layout.firstViewport: At 1440 by 900 with the panel open: list 352px, conversation 672px, panel 416px.
layout.thread: min-height 30dvh (22dvh narrow); side padding clamp(0.75rem, 6%, 4.5rem); bubbles min(36rem, 72%), 86% narrow; pills min(34rem, 85%)
layout.editor: draft grows from 4.5rem to 28dvh (20dvh narrow), then scrolls; the message box area scrolls before the thread gives up its share

zIndex.topLayer: the status panel (popover), the AI dialog and the viewer (modal dialogs)

icons.fill: none (the play triangle in a play disc is filled)
icons.defaultSize: 1.25rem; 1rem in buttons, fields and advice lines; 0.875rem beside small links, on the status pill and in the count chip
icons.brandMark: Separate from the icon set: one drawing on a 48-unit grid, kept once as a symbol in web/assets/brand.svg: a disc in the current colour (set to --brand, so lighter in dark) with a white steering wheel in 4.5-unit strokes with round ends. Used at 2.25rem in the top bar and 5rem in the empty conversation; web/icon.svg is the same drawing in #0073ea for the browser tab.

extensions.theming: Light by default; the navy-based dark values are applied by @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) on the same custom properties in web/css/tokens.css. Roles that differ beyond the palette: bubble-out-meta, segment-on-bg (side, then side-on), segment-on-shadow (shadow-1, then none), photo-ground, the toast pair, the shadows and the scrim. The viewer palette, the photo scrim and the avatar hues are the same in both. No manual switch. Frontmatter lists dark values under the same key with a -dark suffix.
extensions.stylesheets: web/css/tokens.css, base.css, components.css, views.css, utilities.css, in cascade layers tokens, base, components, views, utilities. npm run check-css fails any font size, corner, colour or space outside tokens.css that is not a token.

narrative.overview:
Wheelman is Carbarn's reply assistant, and it looks and behaves like a desktop messaging app with the car beside it. A bar across the top holds the name and the four sections as tabs. Conversations are listed in a column on the left, one conversation is open in the middle, and the car the customer is asking about is on the right. The message box at the bottom of the conversation already holds a suggested reply. That reply is a draft: it is labelled "not sent", it can be edited in place, and the main button only copies it. The car's photos, videos and documents are one press from that draft. Everything on the page supports reading one conversation, checking one draft and putting the right car in it.

The look is quiet and familiar on purpose, in Carbarn's own colours. Bars and columns are white and pale blue, separated by 1px lines and small shifts in tone. The thread sits on a pale blue ground one step deeper than the panels, so the white and blue bubbles read against it. Carbarn's blue marks what is chosen, what is new and what to press. Red, amber and navy appear only as status, always with words beside them. The car photos carry the colour; the interface stays quiet around them, and photos and videos open large in a near-black viewer in both themes, as in any photo app. Text is navy, set in Manrope, the typeface of carbarn.com.au, in sentence case throughout. The one exception is the name: WHEELMAN in Montserrat capitals beside a white steering wheel on a blue disc, with "by Carbarn" under it. Light and dark both ship and follow the computer's setting; the dark theme is built on navy and there is no theme switch.

Density is that of a working tool: 15px body text, 36px controls, 56px bars, 64px list rows, 2px between bubbles from the same sender. Two earlier layouts were rejected by the owner: a page of cards with every customer open at once and coded labels (29 Sep 2026), and a details sidebar of label-value rows with a section switch that took the top of the list (redesigned 16 Oct 2026). This system keeps one conversation and its car in view and says things in words.
keyCharacteristics: A top bar, then three columns in one fixed-height frame: conversation list, open conversation, and the car and customer panel.
The four sections are tabs in the top bar, each with a count; the list column holds only the list.
The suggested reply lives in the message box, never in the thread.
The car is always in view: a photo on the strip above the thread, the full car in the panel, any car through Find a car.
One blue accent, Carbarn's. Red, amber and navy are status colours that always come with words.
Manrope for all text, sentence case, tabular figures. The Montserrat wordmark is the only capitals.
Flat white and pale blue surfaces, 1px dividers, two shadow levels. Photos are the only rich colour.
Pill-shaped controls, 8px corners on bubbles and photos, 16px on the car's main photo and on floating panels, circles for avatars, icon buttons and the mark.
Short motion: 160ms press feedback, 220ms for photos, the draft, the viewer and the tab underline, 260ms for the drawer, none on keyboard moves and none under reduced motion.
Light and a navy-based dark from one set of custom properties; the viewer is dark in both.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Carbarn's blue is the only accent. Solid blue is the primary button, the badges, the wordmark, the mark and the chosen tab's underline, the "checked" dot and the focus ring; the tint with blue text marks things that are on. A second accent hue would break the reading "blue means chosen, new, or press here".

rules.name: The Words With Colour Rule
rules.body: Red, amber and navy never carry meaning alone. Every tinted block holds a plain sentence, every tag is a word ("Check the reply", "Blank to fill", "Needs you"), and each status or availability dot sits beside words that say the same thing.

rules.name: The Paired Tint Rule
rules.body: A status colour is a soft ground with its strong value as text on top, or the strong value as text on a neutral surface. The strong value fills nothing larger than an 8px dot or a 1px underline.

rules.name: The Quiet Frame Rule
rules.body: The car photos are the only rich colour on the page. Around them the interface stays white, pale blue and navy; nothing decorative is tinted to compete with a car.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Every word of interface text is Manrope. Montserrat appears once, at 800, for the wordmark. Both are files in `web/fonts`; the page loads nothing from outside, and falls back to the computer's own sans if a file is missing. Mono appears only for an AI model's name, which the owner may need to type exactly.

rules.name: The Weight Is State Rule
rules.body: 400 is reading text, 500 is a resting name, chip, tab or segment, 650 is emphasis, every heading, and anything selected or unanswered, 700 is kept for badge numerals and the "+N" photo tile, and 800 for the wordmark and the one Undo inside a toast. A name, chip or tab going from 500 to 650 is a state change, always paired with a colour change.

rules.name: The Ink Heading Rule
rules.body: Headings are Navy Ink at 650, in the panel, the status panel and the dialog alike. Blue is for what is chosen, new or pressable, never for a heading.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: The wordmark is the only uppercase text on the page. There are no uppercase labels and no letter-spaced labels. Letter-spacing is only tightened on the headline (-0.02em) and opened by 0.01em on the wordmark, the "by Carbarn" line and avatar initials. Italic is reserved for text the app supplies in place of content: "Photo" or "Attachment" inside a bubble and "writing a suggestion…" in the header.

rules.name: The Docked Draft Rule
rules.body: The suggestion is always in the message box at the bottom of the conversation column. The thread holds only what was really said, plus pills.

rules.name: The Bottom-Anchored Thread Rule
rules.body: The thread opens at its newest message and stays there as the message box grows or new messages arrive, until the user scrolls up more than about 60px. Then a round button appears at the bottom right to return, showing the unanswered count.

rules.name: The Thread Keeps Its Share Rule
rules.body: However tall the message box grows, the conversation keeps 30% of the window (22% narrow). The message box scrolls inside itself before the thread is squeezed further.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: Only these two shadows exist. The bar, columns, headers, rows, chips, tabs and ordinary buttons have none. The panel gets a shadow only when it overlays the conversation; as a grid column it has a 1px line.

dos: Do take every colour, size, space, corner, shadow and duration from `web/css/tokens.css`, give any new colour a light value and a dark value there, and keep `npm run check-css` passing.

Do keep solid blue for the primary button, the badges, the wordmark, the mark and the chosen tab's underline, the "checked" dot and the focus ring, and use Blue Tint with Blue Text for anything that is switched on.
Do set headings in Navy Ink at 650; blue is for what is chosen, new or pressable.
Do show the name as it is built: the white steering wheel on a Carbarn Blue disc, WHEELMAN in Montserrat 800 capitals, and "by Carbarn" under it.
Do put a plain sentence in every red, amber or navy block, and use the strong value as text on its own soft ground.
Do keep the suggested reply in the message box under the label "Suggested reply · not sent", with one filled button: Copy reply, or Send reply in a Marketplace chat.
Do mark blanks in amber and failed figures in red inside the draft text itself, and name each blank on a button that selects it.
Do keep the car in view beside the conversation, and give every photo group, video and document Copy link and Add to reply.
Do put a link into a reply with its label, on a line of its own, typed so Ctrl + Z takes it out.
Do let the photos carry the colour: Photo Ground behind a photo still loading, the soft scrim for anything laid on one, and the near-black viewer in both themes.
Do use the two shadows as they are used now: resting lift for bubbles, pills and the message box; floating for the jump button, the toast, the drawer and the panels that open over the page.
Do give pressable controls the 160ms press scale (0.94 to 0.97) and keep hover styles inside the fine-pointer media query.
Do build content from text nodes and draw new icons on the same 24px grid with a 1.75 stroke and round ends.

Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better against its ground in both themes. The closest pairs are the white label on the primary button in light (about 4.5:1) and, in dark, the primary button under the pointer and the outgoing timestamp (both about 4.9:1).
donts: Don't show the suggestion as a bubble in the thread. The thread is only what was really said.

Don't add anything that looks like sending where nothing is sent. Outside a Marketplace chat there is no send icon and no "Send" label; the button at the bottom right of the message box says what it does, which is copy. In a Marketplace chat the one Send button reads "Send reply", sends exactly the text in the box, waits while a blank is still to be filled, and reads "Sending" until the engine answers.
Don't put the sections back in the list column. They are tabs in the top bar; the list column is the list.
Don't add a second accent colour, and don't use solid red, amber or navy as a fill larger than a status dot.
Don't signal status with colour alone or with a code. Write the words.
Don't add uppercase or letter-spaced labels. The wordmark is the only capitals, and Montserrat belongs to it alone.

Don't add a third typeface or load a font from outside; Manrope and Montserrat are served from `web/fonts`. Don't add a library either. The page loads nothing from outside: car pictures come through Wheelman's own addresses, videos from Carbarn's own storage, and its content security policy forbids inline styles and scripts.
Don't add a third shadow, or put a shadow on the bar, a column, a header, a row, a chip, a tab or an ordinary button.
Don't animate the conversation list when it is moved through with the keyboard. Rows change instantly.
Don't insert customer text as HTML, and don't use real customer names, numbers, messages or cars in examples of this system; use invented ones.
